source.source_file: Statistical Inference (Chapman & Hall_CRC Texts in -- George Casella, Roger L_ Berger -- Texts in Statistical Science, 2ed, 2024.pdf
source.source_limitation_warning: The textbook is authoritative for source-derived mathematical claims. Applied workflows, AI-agent routines, and current software behavior are V2 extensions and must not be presented as author claims.

authority_order: Current generated Statistical Inference Reasoning OS package as draft
governing_statistical_reasoning_rules: State sample space, support, parameter space, and random variables before choosing a method.
Separate estimator, test, interval, model-checking, prediction, and simulation tasks.
Never treat a theorem conclusion as valid without its assumptions and conditions.
Distinguish source-derived definitions/results from applied or AI-agent extensions.
Do not turn likelihood into posterior probability without a prior model.
Do not interpret p-values as probabilities that the null hypothesis is true.
Do not interpret frequentist confidence coverage as posterior probability for a realized interval.
Label asymptotic, bootstrap, and software-dependent conclusions as approximations or current-verification items when appropriate.
For textbook study support, give definitions, assumptions, and proof strategy rather than copied long proofs or solved source exercises.
assumption_checking_checklist: null/alternative and size/level stated for tests
theorem_use_checklist: Locate the theorem/result record by ID.
Read assumptions and conditions before conclusion.
Check connected results and related assumption IDs.
Identify common misuse and reusable risk IDs.
Use the proof summary only as orientation; do not reproduce long proofs.
State what does not follow if assumptions are missing.

estimator_test_interval_distinction.estimator: Constructs or evaluates a statistic/decision rule for a parameter or function of a parameter.
estimator_test_interval_distinction.test: Chooses a rejection rule for specified null/alternative sets and is evaluated by size, level, and power.
estimator_test_interval_distinction.interval: Constructs a random set and evaluates either repeated-sampling coverage or Bayesian posterior probability, depending on construction.

software_current_verification_warnings: Use current documentation for Python/R/Excel statistical functions, GLM/logistic APIs, robust regression APIs, bootstrap routines, optimizers, RNGs, and diagnostics.
Treat package defaults, current API behavior, and simulation reproducibility as time-sensitive.
Consult statistical theorem records for mathematical validity and current-verification flags for implementation validity.
ai_agent_response_standard: Begin by classifying the task and target quantity.
List assumptions before recommending a method.
Cite or name relevant record IDs in internal workflow output.
Ask for missing model/data evidence instead of inventing it.
State interpretation limits and common misuse risks.
Mark applied, AI, or software guidance as extension/current verification where relevant.

compact_context_boundary.scope: Condensed routing layer containing IDs, checks, and risk keys only; full records and traceability remain in component files.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Set operation laws
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: A, B, and C are events on one sample space.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Set expressions can be rearranged without changing the event.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Basic probability consequences
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Complement and bound calculations are valid.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Conditional probability identity
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Conditional probabilities can be computed from joint and marginal probabilities.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Bayes' Rule
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Conditional probabilities can be inverted from P(B|A_i) to P(A_i|B).

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: CDF characterization
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: Function F is real-valued on the real line.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: The function can serve as a distribution function.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Validity of pmfs and pdfs
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: Support and discrete/continuous type are specified.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: The function defines a valid mass/density model.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: One-to-one density transformation
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: X has continuous pdf on support.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: A valid transformed pdf is obtained.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Probability integral transformation
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Uniform random variables can be generated from known continuous distributions and vice versa with inverse cdfs.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: MGF derivatives give moments
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: MGF exists in a neighborhood of zero and derivatives can be taken.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Moments can be computed from the mgf.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Moments and mgfs determine distributions under conditions
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: Moment existence conditions or mgf existence near zero hold as stated.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Distribution equality follows from the stronger moment/mgf conditions.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Leibniz rule for differentiating integrals
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: Limits and integrand are differentiable in θ under stated conditions.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Parameter derivatives of probabilities/normalizing constants can be computed.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Dominated limit interchange for integrals
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Limits can be interchanged with integration.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Differentiating under an integral sign
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Score and moment derivatives can be computed by interchanging operations.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Exponential-family derivative identities
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: Density or pmf has stated exponential-family form.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Moments of sufficient natural statistics can be obtained from normalizing constants.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: General Markov/Chebyshev inequality
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Tail probabilities can be bounded using moments.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Joint factorization and independence
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Independence can be checked through factorization.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Expectation of products under independence
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Product moments can be separated.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: MGF of sum of independent variables
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Distributions of sums can often be identified by transform multiplication.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Law of total expectation
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Hierarchical means can be computed by averaging conditional means.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Conditional variance identity
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Mixture variability splits into within-condition and between-condition components.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Correlation bounds and equality
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Correlation has a bounded standardized interpretation.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Multivariate independence factorization
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Product models and iid likelihoods are valid.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Multivariate MGF factorization
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: Joint mgf exists in a neighborhood of zero for uniqueness/converse uses.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Independence and distributions of sums can be shown through transforms.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Jensen's inequality
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: g is convex on the support.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Expectation inequalities can be derived from convexity.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Sample mean expectation and variance
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: The sample mean is unbiased for μ and becomes less variable at rate 1/n.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Sample variance unbiasedness
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: S² estimates σ² without bias under the model.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Normal sample mean and variance distributions
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Exact finite-sample distributions for mean and variance are available.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Independence of normal sample mean and variance
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Studentized mean has a t distribution because numerator and denominator components are independent.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Derived t and F distributions
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Exact reference distributions for standardized means and variance ratios are obtained.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Joint density of order statistics
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: X_i iid continuous with pdf f.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Order-statistic distributions can be derived from the joint law.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Weak Law of Large Numbers
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: X_i iid with finite mean and variance, as presented in the source's version.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Averages stabilize in probability as sample size grows.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Strong Law of Large Numbers
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: Random sample conditions and moment assumptions as stated in the theorem.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Sample averages converge on almost every infinite sequence.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Central Limit Theorem
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Large-sample normal approximations for sample means are justified.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Slutsky's theorem
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Estimated nuisance quantities can often replace known constants asymptotically.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Delta method
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Uncertainty for smooth transformations can be approximated.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Multivariate delta method
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: Vector statistic has multivariate normal limit.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Approximate variance for functions of multiple estimates can be obtained.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Accept-reject sampling algorithm
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: Target and proposal densities are specified.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Accepted draws have the target distribution.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Sufficiency conditional criterion
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Parameter information in the sample is captured by T in the sufficiency sense.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Factorization theorem
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: The sample has a joint pdf or pmf with common dominating measure as used in the theorem.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Sufficiency can be checked algebraically from the likelihood.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Minimal sufficiency likelihood-ratio criterion
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Minimal sufficient reductions can be identified by comparing likelihood ratios.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Basu's theorem
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: T is complete and sufficient for θ.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Certain information-bearing and information-free summaries are independent.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Completeness in exponential families
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Completeness can be established for many standard models.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Invariance property of MLEs
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: MLE construction commutes with parameter transformation.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Monotonic EM sequence
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: Complete-data and observed-data likelihoods are specified.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: EM provides a likelihood-ascent algorithm, though not necessarily global maximization.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: MSE bias-variance decomposition
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Estimator risk can trade bias against variance.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Cramer-Rao inequality
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: Regularity conditions allow differentiating under the integral/sign.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Sets a lower variance benchmark for unbiased and biased estimators through expectation derivative.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Rao-Blackwell theorem
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Estimators can be improved by using sufficient statistics.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Complete sufficient statistic gives unique BUE
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: UMVU estimators can be found by expressing unbiased estimators through complete sufficient statistics.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Lehmann-Scheffe theorem
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Provides a named theorem for constructing UMVU estimators.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: LRT and sufficiency reduction
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: A sufficient statistic exists through factorization.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Data reduction can simplify test construction without changing LRT evidence.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Neyman-Pearson lemma
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Most powerful tests exist for simple-versus-simple problems.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Karlin-Rubin theorem
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: UMP one-sided tests can be obtained by thresholding T.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Union-intersection test size control
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Complex hypotheses can be tested through a union of rejection regions.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Intersection-union test level control
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: Null is a union of component nulls as stated.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Conservative level control is available for IUTs.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Validity of p-values
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: Large W is more evidence against H0.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Thresholding p-values controls Type I error at the nominal level.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Confidence sets by inverting tests
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: For each θ0, A(θ0) is the acceptance region of a level-α test of H0:θ=θ0.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Confidence sets can be built from hypothesis tests.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Pivotal interval construction
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: Q(X,θ) has distribution independent of unknown parameters.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Intervals inherit exact coverage from the pivot when assumptions hold.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Pivoting a continuous cdf
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Confidence intervals can be constructed without an explicit named pivot.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Pivoting a discrete cdf
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Valid conservative or exact-by-construction intervals can be obtained for discrete parameters/models.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Consistency of MLEs
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: MLEs have large-sample convergence to the true parameter/function.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Asymptotic efficiency of MLEs
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: MLEs are first-order asymptotically efficient in regular models.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Asymptotic distribution of LRT, simple null
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: LRTs can be calibrated approximately by chi-square distributions in large samples.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Asymptotic chi-square LRT for nested composite nulls
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: Random sample from regular parametric model.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Composite LRTs get a general large-sample reference distribution.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Contrasts characterize equal ANOVA means
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: Treatment mean vector θ is defined.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: The classic ANOVA null can be expressed as a collection of contrast hypotheses.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: ANOVA F statistic from supremum of contrast tests
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: ANOVA F logic arises from combining all contrast tests.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Scheffe simultaneous intervals for contrasts
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Family-wise coverage for all contrasts is controlled.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Normal regression estimator distributions
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Exact t/F confidence intervals and tests for regression parameters are available.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Scheffe confidence bands in simple linear regression
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: A whole regression line can be covered, not just individual x points.

active_theorem_capsules_condensed.name: Errors-in-variables slope confidence set
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.check: Errors-in-variables normal model assumptions in Section 12.2.
active_theorem_capsules_condensed.conclusion: Uncertainty about slope can be qualitatively different from ordinary regression.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Defined sample space
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The possible outcomes are specified before events or variables are analyzed.
check: Ask for outcome definitions, measurement resolution, and support.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Events are in the sigma algebra
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The events being assigned probabilities are allowable events in the probability model.
check: For standard real-valued variables use Borel events; for exotic sets request model clarification.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Probability axioms
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The proposed probability rule is nonnegative, normalized, and countably additive.
check: Check nonnegativity, total mass/integral, and additivity for disjoint cases.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Positive conditioning probability
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The event conditioned on has nonzero probability in elementary conditioning.
check: Check whether conditioning is on an event with positive probability or a continuous value requiring conditional density.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Event independence
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: One event's occurrence does not change the probability of the other under the model.
check: Use design, randomization, or joint probabilities to justify; do not infer from disjointness.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Mutual independence
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: All subcollections factor jointly, not merely pairwise.
check: Check sampling design or full joint factorization.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Support restrictions known
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The values where a pmf/pdf is nonzero are stated and respected.
check: Write the support explicitly before integrating, maximizing, or changing variables.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Expectation exists
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The sum or integral defining the expected value is finite/meaningful for the use at hand.
check: Check tail behavior, distribution family, and absolute convergence.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Finite variance
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The second central moment exists and is finite.
check: Check distribution family; be cautious with Cauchy/Pareto tails and outliers.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: MGF exists near zero
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The moment-generating function is finite for t in an open interval around zero.
check: Find the domain of M_X(t) before using derivatives or uniqueness.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Interchange of limit/differentiation and integration
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: A dominating or uniform condition justifies moving limits or derivatives through sums/integrals.
check: Check support dependence, domination, and finite integrals; do not assume automatically.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Monotone/invertible transformation
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The transformation has a well-defined inverse on the relevant support, or support is partitioned into monotone branches.
check: Draw support, solve inverse branches, and include absolute derivative.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Jacobian validity
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The multivariate transformation has a differentiable inverse with nonzero Jacobian on relevant regions.
check: Specify transformed support and compute determinant carefully.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Parametric family membership
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The data-generating distribution is assumed to belong to a specified family indexed by parameters.
check: Use subject matter, diagnostics, residuals, and sensitivity checks; distinguish model from fact.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Full exponential-family open natural parameter set
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The natural parameter vectors cover an open subset of the appropriate Euclidean space.
check: Check natural parameter dimension and whether constraints reduce it.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Location/scale structure
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: Unknown parameters enter only through shifts and/or rescalings of a fixed standard distribution.
check: Standardize data and verify shape invariance under shifts/scales.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Joint distribution specified
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: Multiple variables are modeled together with a joint law, not just separate marginal laws.
check: Ask for joint table/model, sampling design, or dependence assumptions.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Random-variable independence
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The joint distribution of variables factors into marginal distributions.
check: Use design/randomization or factorization; do not infer solely from zero correlation.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Finite second moments for covariance/correlation
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: Covariance and correlation are meaningful only when required second moments and positive standard deviations exist.
check: Check distribution tails, zero-variance variables, and finite sample calculations.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: iid random sample
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: Observations are mutually independent and identically distributed from one population law.
check: Review sampling design, time order, clusters, repeated measures, adaptive sampling, and selection bias.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Normal random sample
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The observations are iid from a normal distribution.
check: Inspect distributional assumptions, residuals, sample size; consider robust or asymptotic alternatives.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Continuous iid sampling for order statistics
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: Order-statistic density formulas assume continuous iid observations without ties.
check: Check for discrete support, ties, censoring, or dependence.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Limit theorem conditions
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The required convergence, moment, and independence conditions hold before using asymptotic approximations.
check: Identify which theorem is being invoked and check its exact assumptions.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Delta-method differentiability
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The transformation is differentiable at the target, with the appropriate nonzero derivative for first-order use.
check: Compute derivative/gradient at the target and inspect boundary cases.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Sufficiency relative to model and parameter
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: A statistic is sufficient only for a stated parameter within a stated model.
check: State f(x|θ), θ, and support before claiming sufficiency.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Minimal sufficiency likelihood ratio conditions
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: Likelihood ratios must be compared carefully where densities/masses are positive and support is handled correctly.
check: Write supports and ratio domains explicitly.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Completeness
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: Zero expectation for every parameter value forces a statistic function to be zero almost surely.
check: Use known complete family theorem or prove the zero-expectation implication.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Ancillarity
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The statistic's distribution is parameter-free.
check: Derive the statistic's distribution under θ or simulate across θ values.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Likelihood matches the actual sampling model
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The likelihood is built from the true or intended joint distribution of the observed data, including the sampling design.
check: State the experiment, sampling plan, observed variables, and missing-data mechanism.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Identifiability
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: Different parameter values lead to different distributions.
check: Check whether parameter constraints or reparameterizations are needed.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: MLE regularity conditions
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The model is smooth, identifiable, and well-behaved enough for consistency and asymptotic normality of MLEs.
check: Check differentiability, support not depending pathologically on θ, interior true parameter, information finite/nonzero, identifiability.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Unbiasedness as a class restriction
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: Best-unbiased results compare only estimators whose expectation equals the target for every parameter value.
check: State whether unbiasedness is required by the problem or just convenient.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Loss function specified
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: An optimal procedure is optimal only relative to a loss/risk criterion.
check: Ask what error costs matter: squared, absolute, 0-1, length, coverage, etc.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Simple hypotheses for Neyman-Pearson
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: Both null and alternative specify single distributions.
check: Identify whether hypotheses are simple, one-sided composite, or two-sided composite.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Monotone likelihood ratio
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The likelihood ratio for ordered parameter values is monotone in a statistic.
check: Derive the statistic's density and ratio; inspect monotonicity.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Size/level control
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: A test's rejection probability under the null is controlled at the nominal level.
check: Compute null distribution exactly, bound it, or simulate under all relevant null values.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Pivot distribution is parameter-free
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: A pivot's distribution does not depend on any unknown parameter.
check: Derive the distribution of Q and check nuisance dependence.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Bayesian prior and posterior model
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: Bayesian procedures require a prior distribution and sampling likelihood.
check: State prior, likelihood, posterior, and sensitivity to prior choices.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Bootstrap resampling model
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: Bootstrap standard errors depend on the resampling scheme approximating the sampling distribution of the estimator.
check: Match resampling scheme to sampling design; compare with analytic/simulation checks.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Simple linear regression error assumptions
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: Regression observations follow a linear mean model with errors satisfying stated distributional assumptions for the intended infe…
check: Inspect residuals, design, heteroscedasticity, independence, leverage, and fixed/random x context.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Oneway ANOVA assumptions
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: Groups follow the ANOVA model with independent normal errors and common variance for exact F inference.
check: Check randomization, independence, group variances, residual normality, and outliers.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Logistic regression Bernoulli model
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: Binary responses follow Bernoulli distributions with probabilities linked to predictors through the logistic curve.
check: Check binary outcome, independence, covariate support, separation, and model form.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Errors-in-variables measurement model
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: Both measured x and y may deviate from latent true values through measurement error.
check: Clarify whether predictors are fixed/measured with error, error variances, independence, and variance ratio.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Outlier or contamination concern
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The analysis acknowledges that a small fraction of observations may be extreme or model-deviating.
check: Inspect residuals/outliers, compare robust and classical estimates, and state contamination model or sensitivity.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Identical distribution in a random sample
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: Each observation has the same marginal distribution.
check: Compare sampling frames, measurement rules, time periods, and covariate shifts.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Parameter space constraints
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The allowed values of the parameter are specified before optimization or testing.
check: State Θ and check whether estimates or null values lie on the boundary.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Finite moments required by the procedure
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The expectations, variances, or higher moments used in a method exist.
check: Check the distribution tail behavior and the exact moment order required.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Minimal sufficiency conditions
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The statistic is sufficient and no coarser sufficient statistic is available under the model criterion.
check: Apply the likelihood-ratio criterion and verify support does not defeat the argument.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Exponential-family form
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The model can be written in the exponential-family form with the stated statistic and natural parameter structure.
check: Write the family in canonical form and check support and natural parameter set.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Null and alternative specification
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The null and alternative parameter sets are stated before a test is evaluated.
check: Identify Θ0, Θ1, one-sided/two-sided form, and nuisance parameters.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Coverage probability target
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The interval procedure is evaluated by the repeated-sampling probability of covering the parameter.
check: State whether the probability is over repeated samples or over a posterior distribution.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Large-sample approximation regime
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The sample size and model regularity are adequate for an asymptotic approximation to be used as an approximation.
check: Check sample size, boundary points, skewness, nuisance parameters, and simulation diagnostics.

active_assumption_capsules_condensed.name: Regression model assumptions
active_assumption_capsules_condensed.meaning: The regression mean, error, variance, independence, and design assumptions match the inference being made.
check: Inspect design, residual patterns, leverage, variance behavior, independence, and outliers.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Method of moments
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Estimate parameters by equating sample moments to model moments.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Maximum likelihood estimation
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Estimate parameters by maximizing the likelihood of the observed sample.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Bayes estimator
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Estimate a parameter under a prior and loss function.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: EM algorithm
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Iteratively maximize likelihood with incomplete or latent data structure.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Mean squared error evaluation
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Evaluate an estimator by expected squared distance from target.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Best unbiased estimation
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Find minimum-variance estimators within the unbiased class.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Rao-Blackwell improvement
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Improve an unbiased estimator by conditioning on a sufficient statistic.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Loss/risk based estimation
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Choose or compare estimators under an explicit loss function.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Unbiasedness evaluation
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Evaluate whether an estimator has expectation equal to the target parameter.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Lehmann–Scheffé logic
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Use a complete sufficient statistic to identify the unique best unbiased estimator.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Likelihood ratio test
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Test hypotheses by comparing best likelihood under null with best likelihood overall.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Bayesian test
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Compare hypotheses using posterior probabilities or posterior expected loss.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Union-intersection test
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Reject a global null when at least one component null is rejected.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Intersection-union test
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Reject a global null only when all component conditions reject.
failure: using UIT when IUT logic is needed

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Size and power evaluation
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Evaluate a test through rejection probabilities under null and alternative values.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Neyman-Pearson most powerful test
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Find the highest-power level-α test for a simple null versus simple alternative.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: p-value calculation and interpretation
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Summarize how extreme the observed statistic is under the null calibration.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Large-sample likelihood-ratio test
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Use chi-square limiting distribution to calibrate an LRT.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Large-sample Wald and score tests
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Use asymptotic normality of estimators or scores to test hypotheses.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Confidence intervals by inverting tests
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Construct a confidence set from parameter values not rejected by tests.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Pivotal interval construction
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Use a parameter-free distribution of Q(X,θ) to solve for θ.
failure: using a statistic with nuisance-dependent distribution

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: CDF pivoting
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Use the distribution function itself as a pivot or confidence-set generator.
failure: assuming exact nominal coverage in discrete models

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Bayesian interval construction
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Construct an interval/credible set from the posterior distribution.
failure: calling it a confidence interval without coverage evaluation

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Coverage probability evaluation
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Evaluate how often a random interval contains the true parameter under repeated sampling.
failure: reporting nominal level without coverage check

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Approximate MLE intervals
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Use asymptotic normality of an MLE to build approximate confidence intervals.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Consistency evaluation
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Check whether an estimator converges in probability to the target.
failure: using consistency to justify small n

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Asymptotic efficiency and ARE
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Compare estimators by limiting variance under asymptotic normality.
failure: choosing by ARE alone under contamination

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Bootstrap standard errors
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Approximate estimator variability by resampling.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: M-estimator
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Estimate by minimizing or solving equations based on a less-sensitive criterion than squared error.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Oneway ANOVA F test
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Test equality of several treatment means under the classic oneway ANOVA model.
failure: post hoc pairwise claims without adjustment

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: ANOVA contrast inference
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Estimate or test planned linear contrasts among treatment means.
failure: testing all pairwise comparisons as if planned

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Simple linear least squares
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Estimate a straight-line mean relationship between response and one predictor.
failure: fitting a line because software can

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: BLUE regression estimation
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Identify best linear unbiased estimators under linear model assumptions.
failure: treating BLUE as robust or causal

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Normal-error regression inference
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Use exact t/F procedures for simple linear regression parameters under normal errors.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Regression prediction interval
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Predict a future response at a specified predictor value with uncertainty.
failure: using mean CI as prediction interval

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Regression confidence bands
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Provide simultaneous uncertainty bands for the fitted mean line.
failure: using pointwise intervals as simultaneous bands

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Errors-in-variables regression
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Model regression when predictor measurements contain error.

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Logistic regression
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Model binary response probabilities with a logistic function of predictors.
failure: linear regression on binary outcomes without checking

active_method_capsules_condensed.name: Robust regression
active_method_capsules_condensed.problem: Fit regression while reducing sensitivity to outliers compared with least squares.
failure: assuming robust fit is automatically valid

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Undefined sample space
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: Probability statements are made before the outcome space and support are declared.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Support mismatch
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: A pmf/pdf/likelihood/test is applied to values outside the model support or with parameter-dependent support ignored.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Discrete-continuous confusion
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: Mass functions, densities, sums, and integrals are interchanged as if they had the same probability meaning.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Treating density as probability
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: A density value is interpreted as P(X=x) rather than as a function integrated over intervals.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Confusing independence and disjointness
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: Mutually exclusive events are treated as independent or independence is asserted because events do not overlap.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Ignored iid assumption
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: Random-sample, likelihood, and sampling-distribution results are used without checking independence and common distribution.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Wrong distribution family
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: A distribution is chosen by name or convenience without checking the sampling story, support, and parameterization.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Missing Jacobian
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: A transformed continuous density is written without the absolute derivative/determinant factor and transformed support.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: MGF nonexistence
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: Moment-generating-function arguments are used when the MGF is not finite in a neighborhood of zero.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Invalid differentiation under integral
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: Derivatives or limits are moved through integrals/sums without domination or regularity conditions.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Sufficiency overclaim
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: A statistic being useful or predictive is confused with sufficiency for a parameter under a specified model.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Likelihood as parameter probability
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: Likelihood is read as a probability distribution over parameters without a prior/posterior model.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Nonunique MLE
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: A likelihood maximum is assumed unique, interior, or numerically stable without checking the parameter space and optimization landscape.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Unbiasedness treated as best
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: Unbiasedness is taken as global optimality while variance, MSE, risk, or loss are ignored.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: p-value as null probability
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: A p-value is interpreted as P(H0 true | data) instead of a tail probability under the null model.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Ignored power
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: A test is judged only by significance/level while the power function and alternatives are not examined.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Size-level confusion
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: The nominal level is treated as guaranteed exact size or size is checked at one parameter point only.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Confidence as posterior probability
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: Frequentist coverage is described as posterior probability for the realized interval without Bayesian assumptions.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Asymptotic overuse
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: Large-sample approximations are used as if exact or reliable without checking sample size, regularity, or boundary cases.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Regression assumption violation
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: Regression/ANOVA/logistic or robust-regression conclusions are made while model, error, design, or outlier assumptions are unexamined.

active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.name: Unverified software defaults
active_reusable_risk_capsules_condensed.description: Current package, spreadsheet, RNG, optimization, or diagnostic defaults are trusted without checking current documentation or code.

diagnostic_question_routing_condensed.question: What is the sample space and what values are actually in the support?
Is this calculation using a mass function, density, cdf, or probability over a set?
Are the events or random variables independent, disjoint, conditionally independent, or merely uncorrelated?
Are the observations plausibly iid, and which part is independence versus identical distribution?
Does the chosen distribution family match the sampling mechanism, support, and parameterization?
For a continuous transformation, what is the transformed support and where is the Jacobian factor?
Does the MGF exist in a neighborhood of zero before using it to identify moments or distributions?
What domination, continuity, or regularity condition justifies moving a derivative or limit through an integral or sum?
Which part of the likelihood depends on the parameter, and what is the parameter space?
Is the statistic sufficient for the parameter under the specified model, and by which criterion?
For minimal sufficiency, does the likelihood-ratio equivalence relation depend on the statistic exactly as required?
Is the statistic being called ancillary, complete, sufficient, or some combination, and for which parameter?
Is the MLE unique, in the parameter space, and at an interior point or boundary?
Do the selected moments exist and identify the parameter values inside the parameter space?
What prior and loss function define the Bayes estimator or Bayesian test?
Is unbiasedness being used as a restriction, or is it being mistaken for overall best performance?
Is the conditioning statistic sufficient, and is the starting estimator unbiased for the target?
Is there a complete sufficient statistic and an unbiased estimator of the target?
What are the null and alternative parameter spaces for the likelihood ratio test?
What are the size, nominal level, and power function of the test?
Is the p-value being interpreted as tail evidence under the null rather than as the probability the null is true?
Are the hypotheses simple enough for the Neyman–Pearson lemma, or is an additional monotonicity/UMP argument needed?
Is the procedure union–intersection or intersection–union, and how is its size or level controlled?
Does the interval claim repeated-sampling coverage or posterior probability?
Is the proposed pivot distribution free of the unknown parameter?
Which acceptance region is being inverted, and what parameter values would not be rejected?
Is the large-sample approximation plausible for this sample size, parameter point, and model regularity?
What resampling model does the bootstrap implementation approximate?
Which loss/ψ function and outlier/contamination concern motivate the M-estimator?
Which ANOVA assumption is doing the most work: independence, normality, equal variance, or treatment structure?
Which regression assumption is doing the most work for this inference: linear mean, independent errors, constant variance, normality, or fixed x design?
Is the response binary/Bernoulli with the stated logit mean model and independent observations?
Are outliers, leverage points, or heavy tails present, and does the robust regression method address the right one?
Are predictor measurements error-free, or is an errors-in-variables model required?
Which software defaults, versions, RNG settings, and optimization tolerances affect the reported statistic?
Does the simulation generator match the target distribution, support, and dependence structure?
Is the request asking for study support rather than a copied proof or solved exercise?
